narrations.en: Step 14 (Final Step): The visual proof is complete! Starting from the definition (assumption) of an isosceles triangle that the lengths of the two sides AB and AC are the same in triangle ABC, which was the starting condition (AB = AC), and passing through the critical auxiliary line of drawing the green angle bisector AD, which divides the vertex angle A exactly in half, to the base BC, it was clearly confirmed that the conclusion was established that the two base angles B and C opposite the two sides of the same length have the same size (angle B = angle C). The key point to remember here is that in order to avoid using the conclusion to be proved (the two base angles are equal) in advance during the proof process, you must draw an auxiliary line bisector of the vertex angles and derive the SAS congruence to avoid falling into circular logic. Finally, ask a deeper question. If, instead of the bisector of the vertex angle, we draw an auxiliary line (median line) connecting the midpoint M of the base BC, under what congruence condition (SSS congruence) can we prove the same?
